Start here
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  'ikon new <name>' creates an app in ./<name>; 'ikon docs convert' prints the playbook for rebuilding an existing React, Next.js, Lovable or Replit app on IKON (its screens are rewritten in C#)
  open
  status · doctor

DEVELOP    make and run the app on this machine
  open

ACCOUNT    who I am and what I own
  login · logout · status · default set · auth refresh | web-sign-in
  auth token create | list | revoke · auth session list | revoke

MACHINE    this computer and the tool itself
  install dotnet | node | git | podman | flutter | android | ios | blender | cad | claude | claude-desktop | codex | antigravity | copilot | cursor | vibe | zcode
  doctor · self update | reset · examples · dev enable | disable
  telemetry status | enable | disable

Global options:

  --app-id <string>                                  App whose token the command runs with
  --dev                                              Run against the development platform
  --prod                                             Run against the production platform
  --version                                          Print the current version of the IKON tool
  --disable-auto-update                              Do not update the tool before the verb runs
  --log-trace                                        Enable trace logging
  --log-debug                                        Enable debug logging

Run 'ikon <verb> --help' for one verb, 'ikon <group>' for a group's verbs, 'ikon help <section>' for a section's
Run 'ikon help env' for the environment variables the tool reads
Use this overview to find a verb or group, then 'ikon help <verb-or-group> --format json' for its contract.
The full inventory is large; save it with 'ikon help --format json --output ikon-help.json' when needed for tooling

result.stdout:
open [ref] [environment]                           Make an app ready to work on here: sign in, download it, check the machine
    [ref] <string>                                     Studio app URL or app id
    [environment] <string>                             Platform the app is on: 'dev' or 'prod' (defaults to your current one)
    --project-dir <string>                             Directory to download the app into (defaults to the current directory)
    --format <string> ("text")                         Output format: auto, text or json (default auto: json when stdout is captured)
    --output <string>                                  Write the output to a file instead of stdout (json/csv only)

  --format json asks nothing and starts no sign-in: a platform this computer
  is not signed in to fails as not-logged-in. A failed download keeps its
  own code, such as conflict when the app's folder is there and not empty.
  It prints {"status": "opened", "folder", "appId", "name", "environment"},
  and what 'ikon doctor' finds goes to stderr.
